title: Full Department Salary Statistics in One Query
description:
Compute the headcount, total salary bill, average salary, maximum salary, and minimum salary for each department in a single query.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `department`, `salary`

Output columns: `department`, `headcount`, `total_salary`, `avg_salary`, `max_salary`, `min_salary`. Order by `department`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineering',95000),(2,'Bob','Engineering',88000),(3,'Carol','Engineering',92000),(4,'Dave','Marketing',72000),(5,'Eve','Marketing',68000),(6,'Frank','Marketing',75000),(7,'Grace','HR',60000),(8,'Henry','HR',58000),(9,'Iris','HR',62000);
solution_sql: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS headcount, SUM(salary) AS total_salary, ROUND(AVG(salary), 0) AS avg_salary, MAX(salary) AS max_salary, MIN(salary) AS min_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY department

test_cases.description: 3 departments: Engineering (3 employees), HR (3 employees), Marketing (3 employees) — 3 rows

hints: All five aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN) can be combined in a single SELECT with one GROUP BY pass.
ROUND(AVG(salary), 0) avoids fractional salaries in the output.
explanation: A single GROUP BY pass computes all aggregates simultaneously. Engineering: headcount=3, total=275000, avg=91667, max=95000, min=88000. Marketing: headcount=3, total=215000, avg=71667, max=75000, min=68000. HR: headcount=3, total=180000, avg=60000, max=62000, min=58000. All in 3 output rows.
